description: pypyr task-runner cli & api for automation pipelines. Automate anything by combining commands, different scripts in different languages & applications into one pipeline process.

summary.one_liner: pypyr is a Python task-runner CLI and API that runs sequential automation pipelines defined in YAML.
summary.what_it_does: pypyr runs pipelines defined in YAML, where each pipeline is a sequence of named steps. Steps can run shell commands, shell pipelines, inline Python, and echo output, and the README names pypyr.steps.cmd, pypyr.steps.shell, pypyr.steps.py, pypyr.steps.echo and pypyr.steps.default as examples. The pipeline syntax supports while loops with a max count, foreach loops, and conditional execution via a run field. Pipelines accept command-line key=value arguments that set context variables used in {placeholder} substitution. The README also says pypyr can read, merge and write configuration files in yaml, json or text.
use_cases: chaining shell commands and scripts into one process
looping over a list of items in an automation sequence
reading, merging and writing yaml or json config files
running pipelines on Linux, macOS, Windows or CI servers
notable: Pipelines are plain YAML files that chain steps without writing Python code
Built-in while and foreach looping and conditional step execution
Command-line arguments set variables that pipelines can substitute into steps
Can run commands, shell pipelines and inline Python in one pipeline
caveats: Requires a Python runtime; the README says it is tested against Python 3.7 and later
Detailed documentation lives on an external docs site, not in the README
keywords: loop over items in a script
